characterization_methods: High-angle annular dark ﬁ eld imaging (HAADF)
evidence: Films deposited on Si wafer were characterized by X-ray reﬂ ectivity (XRR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDXS), as well as atomic force microscopy (AFM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The present ALD process was used to coat CNTs and boron nitride nanotubes. The coated CNTs were characterized by SEM and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns have been recorded on a 35-nm-thick ﬁ lm deposited on Si wafer and on coated CNTs. The AFM measurements were performed using a commercial NTEGRA Prima setup (NT-MDT) in tapping mode. XRD characterization of ﬁ lms on Si wafers and CNTs was performed with a Philips X’Pert MRD X’ray diffractometer. Coated wafers were further analyzed by SEM and EDXS using a SU-70 (Hitachi) microscope. The AFM measurements were performed using a commercial NTEGRA Prima setup (NT-MDT) in tapping mode. The XPS experiments were performed on thick ﬁ lms in an ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) multipurpose surface analysis system. The coated nanosubstrates were characterized by HR-TEM and STEM using a JEOL JEM-2200FS microscope. Electron energy loss spectra (EELS) were recorded from the coated boron nitride nanotubes.
